examples.ko: 날씨가 이번 주말 행사의 성패를 좌우할 것 같아요.
examples.en: The weather seems likely to decide whether this weekend's event succeeds or fails.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트의 성패는 팀워크에 달려 있어요.
examples.en: The success or failure of this project depends on teamwork.
Do you think first impressions decide the outcome of an interview?

examples.ko: 너무 성패에 신경 쓰지 말고 즐겨 보세요.
examples.en: Don't worry too much about success or failure, and just enjoy it.

examples.ko: 장사의 성패는 가게 위치에서 갈린다고들 해요.
examples.en: They say the success of a business is decided by the shop's location.

examples.ko: 이 계획이 회사의 성패를 가를 중요한 시험대예요.
examples.en: This plan is an important test that will make or break the company.

explain: '성공과 실패'를 한 단어로 묶은 말이라서 '성패를 좌우하다', '성패가 달려 있다', '성패를 가르다'처럼 결과가 갈리는 상황에 자주 써요. 일이 이미 성공했는지 말할 때보다 앞으로 어떻게 될지 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It packs 'success and failure' into one word, so it fits phrases like '성패를 좌우하다', '성패가 달려 있다' and '성패를 가르다', where the result could go either way. It sounds more natural when talking about what will happen than about something that has already succeeded.

examples.ko: 어제 열린 시장 행사가 성황을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: The market event held yesterday was a great success.
I'm so happy the concert ended with a packed, successful crowd.
The shop's opening ceremony was a big, crowded success.

examples.ko: 공연이 매일 성황이라서 표 구하기가 어려워요.
examples.en: The show is packed every day, so tickets are hard to get.

examples.ko: 동네 축제가 성황 속에 막을 내렸어요.
examples.en: The neighborhood festival came to an end amid a lively turnout.
It's a small shop, but it's always busy with customers.

explain: 행사, 공연, 가게처럼 사람이 많이 모여서 잘되는 모습을 말해요. '성황을 이루다'와 '성황리에 끝나다'가 가장 많이 쓰이고, 사람이 없을 때는 반대로 '썰렁하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes events, shows and shops that draw a big crowd and go well. The most common forms are '성황을 이루다' and '성황리에 끝나다'. When nobody shows up, people say '썰렁하다' instead.

examples.en: That discovery is regarded as an event of world-historical importance.

examples.ko: 세계사적 관점에서 보면 그 전쟁의 의미가 달라져요.
examples.en: From a world-history perspective, the meaning of that war changes.

examples.ko: 세계사적인 변화가 우리 생활에도 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: World-historical changes also affect our daily lives.

examples.ko: 이 유적은 세계사적 가치가 높다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this site has great value in world history.

examples.ko: 세계사적 흐름을 알아야 뉴스가 더 잘 이해돼요.
examples.en: If you know the flow of world history, the news makes more sense.

examples.ko: 선생님이 세계사적 의미가 큰 사건을 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained an event with great significance in world history.

explain: '세계사적 사건', '세계사적 의미'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 말이에요. 한 나라가 아니라 세계 전체의 역사에서 볼 때 크다는 느낌이라 뉴스나 수업, 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun, as in '세계사적 사건' or '세계사적 의미'. It carries the feeling of being big not just for one country but for the history of the whole world, so it shows up mostly in news, lessons and writing.

examples.en: The team started a generational turnover this season.

examples.ko: 회사 임원진의 세대교체가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: The generational change among the company's executives is moving quickly.
Talk of generational change often comes up in politics.

examples.ko: 우리 가게도 이제 세대교체를 할 때가 됐어요.
examples.en: It's time for our shop to hand things over to the next generation, too.
The atmosphere changed a lot once the generations turned over.
The national team that succeeded in renewing its players won the title.

explain: 스포츠 팀, 회사, 정치처럼 나이 든 사람들이 물러나고 젊은 사람들이 자리를 맡는 상황에 많이 써요. '세대교체를 하다', '세대교체가 이루어지다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used for sports teams, companies and politics, when older people step aside and younger people take over. You can say '세대교체를 하다' or '세대교체가 이루어지다'.

examples.en: He sang a serenade beneath her window.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 모차르트의 세레나데 중에서 가장 유명해요.
examples.en: This piece is the most famous of Mozart's serenades.
A serenade concert is held in the park in the evening.
I prepared a serenade for my love confession.

examples.ko: 세레나데는 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래예요.
examples.en: A serenade is a song you sing to your lover at night.

examples.ko: 기타 반주에 맞춰 세레나데를 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm practicing a serenade to a guitar accompaniment.

explain: 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래를 뜻하기도 하고, 클래식에서는 '소야곡'이라고도 하는 곡 종류를 가리켜요. 일상 대화보다는 음악 이야기나 낭만적인 장면에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: It can mean a song sung to a lover at night, and in classical music it is a type of piece also called '소야곡'. You hear it more in talk about music or romantic scenes than in everyday conversation.

examples.en: This outfit is simple, but you can feel its sophistication.
That café stands out for the refinement of its interior.
It has a sophisticated design, so it's very popular.
If you cut down on colors, the elegance actually comes through.
Refinement shows in the way she speaks.

examples.ko: 가구 배치만 바꿔도 방에 세련미를 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Just rearranging the furniture can give the room a touch of sophistication.

explain: '세련되다'가 상태라면 '세련미'는 그 안에서 느껴지는 멋을 말해서 '세련미가 느껴지다', '세련미가 돋보이다'처럼 자주 써요. 옷, 디자인, 말투, 공간에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: If '세련되다' describes a state, '세련미' is the stylish quality you feel in it, so you often hear '세련미가 느껴지다' and '세련미가 돋보이다'. It works for clothes, design, speech and spaces.

examples.en: The doctor examined the patient's condition closely.
Please read the contract carefully, down to the details.

examples.ko: 지도를 세밀히 그리는 데 이틀이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took two days to draw the map in detail.
They are investigating the cause of the accident thoroughly.
When I looked closely, there was a small scratch.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 글을 세밀히 고쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher corrected my writing in fine detail.

explain: '자세히'보다 작은 부분까지 꼼꼼하게 본다는 느낌이 강하고, 조사하다·살피다·검토하다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 평소 대화에서는 '자세히'나 '꼼꼼히'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '자세히', it feels more like checking even the smallest parts, and it pairs well with verbs like 조사하다, 살피다 and 검토하다. In casual talk people more often say '자세히' or '꼼꼼히'.

examples.ko: 세밑이 가까워 오니 고향에 가고 싶은 마음이 간절해져요.
examples.en: As the end of the year draws near, I long more and more to go home.
The expressways are very congested at the end of the year.

examples.ko: 올해 세밑은 가족과 조용히 보낼 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to spend this year's end quietly with my family.

examples.ko: 세밑 분위기 때문인지 거리가 들떠 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of the year-end mood, the streets look excited.

examples.ko: 세밑에 이웃을 돕는 모금 활동이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many fundraising drives to help neighbors at the end of the year.
I called to give you my year-end greetings in advance.

explain: 한 해가 끝나 가는 12월 말쯤을 가리키고, '연말'보다 글이나 뉴스에서 좀 더 운치 있게 들려요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '연말'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It points to the last days of December as the year ends, and it sounds a bit more literary than '연말' in writing and news. In everyday conversation people usually just say '연말'.

examples.en: I think the customer groups need to be broken down further.
Market segmentation is the basis of marketing.
Thanks to the division of tasks into smaller parts, work got faster.
If the subdivision goes too far, things actually get complicated.
Jobs are becoming more and more specialized.
The students asked for the lesson content to be broken into finer parts.

explain: 하나를 여러 작은 부분으로 나눈다는 뜻이라서 시장, 업무, 직업, 등급처럼 큰 덩어리가 대상일 때 잘 써요. '세분화가 되다'보다 '세분화가 필요하다', '세분화가 진행되다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means splitting one big thing into many smaller parts, so it suits targets like markets, tasks, jobs and grades. People more often say '세분화가 필요하다' or '세분화가 진행되다' than '세분화가 되다'.

examples.en: Break the problem down into small parts and solve it.
The school divides students into finer groups by level.
If you divide the team in detail by role, work gets easier.
Please don't split the menu into too many categories.
The app has divided the notification types into finer categories.
I'm going to break the budget down by item.

explain: '나누다'보다 이미 나눈 것을 더 잘게 쪼갠다는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 세분화하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 분류·업무·예산·시장처럼 체계가 있는 대상에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '나누다', it feels like cutting something already divided into finer pieces. It is used as '~을/를 세분화하다' and suits organized things such as categories, tasks, budgets and markets.

examples.en: How nice would it be if everything in life went my way?
My grandfather is interested in everything under the sun.

examples.ko: 가끔은 세상만사가 다 귀찮을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel bothered by everything in the world.
They say everything depends on your state of mind, don't they?

examples.ko: 퇴근하고 나니 세상만사가 다 편안해 보여요.
examples.en: After leaving work, everything in the world looks peaceful.

examples.ko: 친구랑 세상만사 이야기를 하다 보니 밤이 깊었어요.
examples.en: Talking about all sorts of things with my friend, the night grew late.

explain: '세상의 모든 일'이라는 뜻이라서 '세상만사가 귀찮다', '세상만사 다 잊고 쉬고 싶다'처럼 지치거나 편안한 기분을 말할 때 자주 써요. '세상만사 마음먹기에 달렸다'는 한 덩어리로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It covers all the affairs of the world, so people use it to express moods, as in '세상만사가 귀찮다' (I'm sick of everything) or '세상만사 다 잊고 쉬고 싶다' (I want to forget everything and rest). The saying '세상만사 마음먹기에 달렸다' is also often used as a set phrase.

examples.ko: 세상살이가 쉽지 않다는 걸 요즘 느껴요.
examples.en: These days I'm realizing that life isn't easy.
My grandmother often tells me stories about life.

examples.ko: 세상살이에 지칠 때 저는 산책을 해요.
examples.en: When I'm worn out by life, I go for a walk.

examples.ko: 사회 초년생에게 세상살이는 모든 게 낯설어요.
examples.en: For someone new to working life, everything about the world feels unfamiliar.
I learned a lot of life wisdom from books.

examples.ko: 세상살이 다 그런 거예요, 너무 속상해하지 마세요.
examples.en: That's just how life is, so don't be too upset.

explain: '인생'이 더 큰 흐름이라면 '세상살이'는 사람들 사이에서 먹고 살고 부딪히는 일상의 어려움이나 이치를 말할 때 많이 써요. 어른들이 '세상살이가 다 그렇다'고 위로하듯 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: If '인생' is the larger course of a life, '세상살이' is more about the everyday struggles and ways of living among other people. Older people often use it to console someone, as in '세상살이가 다 그렇다'.

examples.en: The teacher explained the rules in detail.
I wrote down the travel schedule in detail.
Please check the receipt item by item.

examples.ko: 그는 사고 상황을 세세히 기억하고 있어요.
examples.en: He remembers the details of the accident clearly.
If you go over every little detail, it's tiring.
The instructions explain how to use it in great detail.

explain: '세밀히'처럼 꼼꼼하다는 뜻이지만, 하나하나 작은 항목까지 빠뜨리지 않는 느낌이 더 강해요. 설명하다·적다·기억하다처럼 내용을 풀어내는 말과 자주 써요.
explain_en: Like '세밀히' it means thorough, but it stresses not skipping any small item one by one. It often goes with verbs of laying out content, such as 설명하다, 적다 and 기억하다.

examples.en: He doesn't have much worldly greed.
Worldly success is not the only form of happiness.

examples.ko: 스님은 세속적인 일에서 멀리 떨어져 살아요.
examples.en: The monk lives far away from worldly affairs.
Don't judge people by worldly standards.

examples.ko: 저는 돈이나 명예 같은 세속적 가치에 매달리지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't cling to worldly values like money and fame.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 세속적인 사랑을 그리고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel depicts earthly love.

explain: 종교나 정신적인 것과 달리 돈, 명예, 성공처럼 현실 세상의 가치를 말해요. '속물적'처럼 비판하는 느낌으로 쓸 때도 있고, 단순히 '현실적인'이라는 뜻으로 쓸 때도 있어서 문맥을 봐야 해요.
explain_en: As opposed to religion or the spiritual, it refers to the values of the real world, such as money, fame and success. Sometimes it sounds critical, like '속물적', and sometimes it simply means 'worldly', so you need to read the context.

examples.ko: 정월 대보름에 부럼을 깨물고 달집을 태우는 것도 세시 풍속이에요.
examples.en: Cracking nuts and burning the moon house on the first full moon is also a seasonal custom.

examples.ko: 동지에 팥죽을 먹는 세시 풍속은 지금도 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The seasonal custom of eating red bean porridge on the winter solstice continues today.

examples.ko: 양력을 채택하면서 세시 풍속도 변화를 겪었어요.
examples.en: Seasonal customs also changed when the solar calendar was adopted.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 세시 풍속 체험 행사를 열어요.
examples.en: The museum holds an event to experience seasonal customs.

examples.ko: 설날에 먹는 떡국도 대표적인 세시 음식이에요.
examples.en: The tteokguk eaten at Seollal is also a typical seasonal food.

examples.ko: 할머니께서 세시 풍속을 하나씩 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother taught me the seasonal customs one by one.

explain: 거의 '세시 풍속', '세시 음식'처럼 설날, 대보름, 단오, 추석 같은 철마다 되풀이되는 전통 행사 이야기에서 써요. 시계의 '세 시(3시)'와는 전혀 다른 말이고, 띄어 쓰는 '세 시'는 시간이에요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in '세시 풍속' and '세시 음식', when talking about traditional events that repeat each season, such as Seollal, Daeboreum, Dano and Chuseok. It has nothing to do with '세 시' (three o'clock), which is written with a space and means a time.

examples.en: Please watch your child's changes attentively.
The clerk wrapped the clothes with great care.
He attentively took care of the guests' requests.
Thanks to the careful preparation, the presentation went well.
Thank you for reviewing the manuscript so carefully.

examples.ko: 친구가 선물을 세심히 고르는 모습이 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was grateful to see my friend choosing the gift with such care.

explain: '꼼꼼히'가 빠뜨리지 않는 것이라면 '세심히'는 상대를 배려하는 마음이 담긴 주의 깊음에 가까워요. 그래서 살피다·챙기다·배려하다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: If '꼼꼼히' is about not missing anything, '세심히' is closer to attentiveness that carries consideration for others. That is why it goes well with verbs such as 살피다, 챙기다 and 배려하다.

examples.en: How much is the tax I have to pay this year?
The tax amount differs depending on income.
The tax amount is written separately on the receipt.
If you get deductions, the tax amount goes down.

examples.ko: 세액을 계산해 주는 프로그램을 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a program that calculates the tax amount.

examples.ko: 신고서에 세액을 잘못 적어서 다시 냈어요.
examples.en: I wrote the wrong tax amount on the return, so I filed it again.

explain: '세금'은 세금 전체를 말하고, '세액'은 실제로 내야 하는 금액 숫자를 가리켜서 계산서, 신고서, 영수증에서 많이 보여요. '세액 공제'처럼 세금 용어와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '세금' is tax in general, while '세액' is the actual number you have to pay, so you see it on invoices, tax returns and receipts. It often appears in tax terms such as '세액 공제' (tax credit).

examples.en: My monthly salary is 3 million won before tax.
There is a big gap between the pretax annual salary and what you take home.
Be sure to ask whether it's before tax or after tax.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 세전 수익이 20퍼센트 늘었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this company's pretax profit grew by 20 percent.

examples.ko: 이 금액은 세전이라서 실제로 받는 돈은 더 적어요.
examples.en: This amount is pretax, so what you actually receive is less.
The menu showed pretax prices, so it was confusing.

explain: 월급이나 연봉, 가격이 세금을 빼기 전 금액이라는 뜻으로 써서 '세전 월급', '세전 연봉'처럼 말해요. 반대말은 '세후'이고, 실제로 받는 돈은 '실수령액'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It marks a salary or price as the amount before taxes are taken out, as in '세전 월급' and '세전 연봉'. The opposite is '세후', and the money you actually receive is called '실수령액'.

examples.ko: 과일 세척제를 써서 농약을 씻어 냈어요.
examples.en: I used a fruit wash to rinse off the pesticide.

examples.ko: 세척제는 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep the cleaning product out of children's reach.
This cleaner works well on greasy stains.
I bought a new bathroom cleaner.

examples.ko: 세척제를 너무 많이 쓰면 헹구기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you use too much cleaner, it's hard to rinse off.
I wash the baby bottles with bottle cleanser.

explain: '세제'가 빨래나 설거지처럼 넓게 쓰는 말이라면 '세척제'는 과일, 젖병, 욕실, 기계처럼 씻어 내는 대상에 맞춘 제품에 많이 붙여요. 제품 이름이나 설명에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: While '세제' is a broad word for laundry or dish detergent, '세척제' is often attached to products made for a specific target, such as fruit, baby bottles, bathrooms or machines. You often see it in product names and descriptions.

examples.ko: 그는 세파에 시달리며 오랫동안 일해 왔어요.
examples.en: He has worked for a long time, battered by life's hardships.

examples.ko: 세파에 휘둘리지 않고 중심을 지키고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to keep my balance without being tossed around by life's hardships.
After going through life's hardships, he became a stronger person.

examples.ko: 아직 세파에 물들지 않은 아이의 웃음이에요.
examples.en: It's the smile of a child not yet touched by the harshness of the world.
Even when life is rough, I hold on because I have my family.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 세파를 이겨 낸 이야기를 해 주세요.
examples.en: My grandfather tells stories of how he overcame life's hardships.

explain: 원래는 '세상의 물결'이라는 비유라서 '세파에 시달리다', '세파에 휘둘리다', '세파를 겪다'처럼 힘든 세상살이를 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 일상 대화보다는 글이나 어른들의 이야기에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It started as a metaphor for the 'waves of the world', so it is used for the hardships of life, as in '세파에 시달리다', '세파에 휘둘리다' and '세파를 겪다'. You hear it more in writing and in older people's stories than in light everyday talk.
